heading: 🧬 Welcome to genekitr!
text: book practical tutorial searching gene information, converting gene, protein, probe identifiers, performing gene enrichment analysis, creating publication-ready plots.new R, worry. book provides plenty example code help get started. reading book, able perform enrichment analyses create informative plots using data.

heading: 🍱 Content
text: Part 1 (Search Information) shows search gene metadata PubMed articles.Part 2 (ID Conversion) describes identifier conversion among gene symbols aliases, NCBI Entrez Gene IDs, Ensembl IDs, UniProt IDs, microarray probe IDs.Part 3 (Enrichment Analysis) introduces gene sets two widely used functional enrichment methods: -representation analysis (ORA) functional class scoring (FCS).Part 4 (Plotting) includes 13 plots ORA results, 5 plots FCS-GSEA results, 2 Venn diagrams, 1 volcano plot.

heading: 1 Quick start
text: section helps quickly get sense function works. Click titles view details.

heading: 1.1 Installation
text: genekitr requires R >= 4.0. Annotation data downloaded first use cached tools::R_user_dir("genekitr", "data") (gene sets geneset cached way), later runs need internet connection.
code:
# stable version from CRAN
install.packages("genekitr")
# development version from GitHub
remotes::install_github("GangLiLab/genekitr")

heading: 1.2 Search gene metadata
code:
id <- c("MCM10", "CDC20", "S100A9", "MMP1", "BCC7","FAKEID","HBD", "NUDT10")
info <- genInfo(id, org = "hs")
# keep unique records
info2 <- genInfo(id, org = "hs", unique = TRUE)
# supports both hg19 and hg38 genome build versions
v19 <- genInfo(id, org = "hs",hgVersion = "v19")
v38 <- genInfo(id, org = "hs",hgVersion = "v38")

heading: 1.3 Search PubMed records
code:
term <- c("Tp53", "Brca1", "Tet2")
add_term <- c("stem cell", "mouse")
l <- getPubmed(term, add_term, num = 30)

# set "num" to a larger value to get all the records
all <- getPubmed(term, add_term, num = 666666)

heading: 1.8 ORA analysis (over-representation analysis)
code:
# 1st step: get input IDs
id <- c("TP53","BRCA1", "PD1", "PDL1")
# 2nd step: get gene set
gs <- geneset::getGO(org = "human",ont = "mf")
# 3rd: analysis
ego <- genORA(id,
              geneset = gs,
              p_cutoff = 0.05,
              q_cutoff = 0.05
)

heading: 1.9 FCS GSEA analysis
text: FCS stands “functional-class-scoring”.geneList pre-ranked gene list ordered decreasing order. Input IDs can Entrez, Ensembl, Symbol, UniProt IDs.
code:
# 1st step: get pre-ranked gene list
data(geneList, package = "genekitr")
# 2nd step: get gene set
gs <- geneset::getGO(org = "human",ont = "mf")
# 3rd: analysis
gse <- genGSEA(genelist = geneList, 
               geneset = gs,
               p_cutoff = 0.05,
               q_cutoff = 0.05)

heading: 1.10.2 Import clusterProfiler result
code:
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
data(geneList, package="DOSE")
gene <- names(geneList)[abs(geneList) > 2]

## GO result from clusterProfiler
go <- enrichGO(gene          = gene,
                OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
                ont           = "BP",
                pAdjustMethod = "BH",
                pvalueCutoff  = 0.01,
                qvalueCutoff  = 0.05)
## GSEA result from clusterProfiler
kk <- gseKEGG(geneList     = geneList,
               organism     = 'hsa',
               minGSSize    = 120,
               pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
               verbose      = FALSE)
## Other ORA results from clusterProfiler 
# (e.g. KEGG/DOSE/WikiPathways...)
do <- enrichDO(gene          = gene,
              ont           = "HDO",
              pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
              pAdjustMethod = "BH",
              universe      = names(geneList),
              minGSSize     = 5,
              maxGSSize     = 500,
              qvalueCutoff  = 0.05)

## Convert clusterProfiler results into genekitr format
go_easy <- importCP(go, type = "go")
kk_easy <- importCP(kk,type = 'gsea')
do_easy <- importCP(do,type = 'other')

heading: 1.11 Plot ORA
text:
Supported types include: bar, wego, bubble, dot, lollipop, geneheat, genechord,
network, gomap, goheat, gotangram, wordcloud, upset two-group barplot
code:
plotEnrich(ego, plot_type = "dot")
plotEnrich(ego, plot_type = "bar")
plotEnrich(ego, plot_type = "geneheat")
plotEnrich(ego, plot_type = "network", scale_ratio = 0.5)

heading: 1.12 Plot GSEA
text: Supported types include: volcano, classic, fgsea, ridge bar
code:
plotGSEA(gse, plot_type = "volcano", show_pathway = 3)

genes <- c("MET", "TP53", "PMM2")
plotGSEA(gse, plot_type = "classic", show_pathway = 3, show_gene = genes)

plotGSEA(gse, plot_type = "fgsea", show_pathway = 3)

heading: 1.13 Plot Venn
code:
set1 <- paste0(rep("gene", 100), sample(1:1000, 100))
set2 <- paste0(rep("gene", 100), sample(1:1000, 100))
set3 <- paste0(rep("gene", 100), sample(1:1000, 100))

# Classic Venn plot
plotVenn(list(gset1 = set1, gset2 = set2, gset3 = set3), use_venn = TRUE)
# UpSet plot
plotVenn(list(gset1 = set1, gset2 = set2, gset3 = set3), use_venn = FALSE)

heading: 1.14 Plot DEG Volcano
code:
data(deg, package = "genekitr")
plotVolcano(deg, "p.adjust",
  remove_legend = T,
  show_gene = c("CD36", "DUSP6", "IER3", "CDH7")
)

heading: 2 Search gene metadata
text: genInfo() function helps users quickly search batch gene metadata, gene names, genomic location, GC content, .
